headline: Chips Anchor a Wobbly Market as Fair Isaac's Collapse Commands the Floor
body_html:
Wednesday's mid-session tape is running unevenly, with 301 names lower against 240 higher across our 544-stock universe. Semiconductors are the lone sector in the green, up 1.06%, while every other group trades in the red — Materials and Energy trailing the pack with losses of 0.89% and 0.80%, respectively. The tone is defensive without being panicked, as investors appear content to rotate rather than retreat.

The session's defining story is Fair Isaac, whose shares have cratered 26.52% midday, making it by far the most dramatic single-name move on either side of the ledger. The financial-data firm is trading in isolation on the downside, while semiconductor-equipment names are driving the bright spot: Onto Innovation is up 5.52% and Applied Materials has gained 5.19%, lending credibility to the chip sector's outperformance. Bloom Energy is also surging 10.80%, though energy stocks overall remain under pressure.

Into the close, watch whether the semiconductor rally can hold as Micron's after-bell earnings approach — traders are known to trim exposure ahead of the print. Holiday retail headlines projecting sales topping one trillion dollars offer a modest tailwind for consumer names, though that sector still sits fractionally negative at midday. Fair Isaac's trajectory into the final hour will also be closely monitored for any sign of stabilization.

briefs.headline: Fair Isaac Suffers Steep Intraday Slide
briefs.body: Shares of Fair Isaac have tumbled 26.52% by midday, making it the sharpest single-name decline in the session by a wide margin. No other decliner comes close in magnitude. The move has drawn significant attention across trading desks, with the financial-data company's selloff rippling through sentiment in the broader Financial-Data space.

briefs.headline: Chip-Equipment Names Power Sector to Top Spot
briefs.body: Semiconductors are the only sector posting a gain Wednesday, rising 1.06% at midday. Onto Innovation and Applied Materials are leading the charge, up 5.52% and 5.19% respectively. The strength comes ahead of Micron's post-close earnings report, which traders are watching closely for cues on the broader chip demand cycle.

briefs.headline: Bloom Energy Surges Against a Weak Energy Tape
briefs.body: Bloom Energy has jumped 10.80% midday, standing out sharply against an energy sector that is otherwise down 0.80%. The fuel-cell company's rally is the second-largest gain in the entire universe today. Its move higher is notable precisely because metallurgical coal and oil-services names are among the session's steeper losers.

briefs.headline: Metallurgical Coal Stocks Hit by Broad Pressure
briefs.body: Alpha Metallurgical Resources and Warrior Met Coal are both deep in the red, falling 5.43% and 4.05% respectively. Their declines are dragging the Materials sector down 0.89%, the weakest reading across all groups tracked today. Steel Dynamics is also off 3.69%, adding to the sector's rough afternoon.

briefs.headline: Mattel Installs New Chief Executive
briefs.body: Toy giant Mattel has named Roger Lynch as its incoming chief executive, replacing longtime leader Ynon Kreiz. The management change marks a significant strategic inflection point for one of the world's most recognized consumer brands. Investors will be watching for any early signals on Lynch's operating priorities in the quarters ahead.

briefs.headline: Ken Griffin Commits $3 Billion to Carnegie Mellon
briefs.body: Hedge fund titan Ken Griffin has pledged three billion dollars to Carnegie Mellon University, described as a historic philanthropic commitment to the institution. The gift is among the largest ever directed at a single university and is expected to fund research and academic programs across the school's engineering and technology disciplines.
